title: Geometric abelian subvarieties have a finite separable field of definition
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], fix an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Let $C\hookrightarrow A_\Omega$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] which is an abelian variety over $\Omega$. There exist an intermediate field $k\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$ with $E/k$ finite Galois (finite-dimensional, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal, meaning that every minimal polynomial over $k$ of an element of $E$ splits in $E$), and a closed abelian subvariety $C_E\hookrightarrow A_E$, such that $(C_E)_\Omega=C$ as closed subgroup schemes of $A_\Omega$. Base changes are those of [def-pc-base-change]. No perfectness hypothesis on $k$ is made.

source.place: I Proposition 10.1 footnote 10, p.42, and discussion after Remark 10.2 footnote 11, p.43: missing imperfect-field prerequisite. Explicit source: Milne, Abelian Varieties (January 2, 2022), https://www.jmilne.org/math/xnotes/AVs.pdf, Section 12, second unnumbered lemma after Proposition 12.1, printed p.19 (finite separable definition); replacing its finite separable extension by its finite normal closure gives the finite Galois form. This newer article is WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Let $k_s\subseteq\Omega$ consist of the elements separable over $k$; by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] it is a subfield, separable algebraic over $k$ and separably closed, hence a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. In particular $k_s/k$ is Galois: the roots in $\Omega$ of the minimal polynomial of a separable element are again separable. By [lem-sfb-abelian-prime-to-torsion-dense], $T=\bigcup_{n\geq1,\,n\in k^\times}C[n](\Omega)$ is dense in $C$. Because $C\hookrightarrow A_\Omega$ is a group homomorphism, every point in $C[n](\Omega)$ lies in $A[n](\Omega)$. The finite etale scheme $A[n]$ is given by [lem-sc-mult-n-etale-kernel]; its coordinate algebra is a product of finite separable extensions of $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. Every $k$-map from one of these factors to $\Omega$ has image in $k_s$. Thus every point of $T$ is the scalar extension of a point of $A(k_s)$.

source.place: I Section 10, pp.42–45, supporting torsion inputs; agent expansion of the missing separable-definition argument. Explicit comparison: Milne 2022, Section 12, second unnumbered lemma after Proposition 12.1, printed p.19 (WANTED).

proof.text: The abelian variety $C$ is smooth, so it is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. The scheme $A_{k_s}$ is an abelian variety by [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], hence finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-rational-closed-subscheme-descent] with $F=k_s$, $L=\Omega$, $X=A_{k_s}$, $Z=C$ and the set of $k_s$-points found in step 1. Obtain a closed subscheme $D\hookrightarrow A_{k_s}$ with $D_\Omega=C$. Choose a finite affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $A$, possible since $A$ is proper, hence finite type. Each $R_i\otimes_k k_s$ is a finite-type algebra over a field and is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Therefore the ideal $I_i$ cutting out $D$ on $(U_i)_{k_s}$ has finitely many generators. Write each generator as a finite sum $\sum_j r_j\otimes a_j$ and collect the finitely many coefficients $a_j\in k_s$ across the finitely many charts.

source.place: I Section 10, pp.42–45, supporting torsion inputs; agent expansion of the missing separable-definition argument. Explicit comparison: Milne 2022, Section 12, second unnumbered lemma after Proposition 12.1, printed p.19 (WANTED).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] to that finite coefficient set inside the Galois extension $k_s/k$. Obtain $k\subseteq E\subseteq k_s$ finite Galois. In $R_i\otimes_k E$ let $J_i$ be generated by the same displayed finite sums. Its extension to $R_i\otimes_k k_s$ is $I_i$. These ideals agree on overlaps: on any affine open $W\subseteq (U_i)_E\cap(U_j)_E$, their extensions to $W_{k_s}$ agree, since both cut out $D$. For an $E$-vector space $V$, the map $V\to V\otimes_E k_s$ is injective (extend any nonzero vector to a basis); apply this to the quotients by the two ideals to reflect both ideal inclusions. The ideals thus glue to a closed subscheme $C_E\hookrightarrow A_E$, with $(C_E)_{k_s}=D$ and $(C_E)_\Omega=C$ as closed subschemes.

source.place: Tags 09DT/0EXM, lemma-normal-closure/lemma-normal-closure-galois; coefficient construction and ideal reflection as in Milne algebraic groups, Appendix A.65.

proof.text: The group operations of $A_E$ restrict to $C_E$. Indeed, the composite $C_E\times_E C_E\to A_E$ becomes the multiplication into $C$ after extension to $\Omega$. On each affine chart every element of the ideal of $C_E$ therefore maps to zero after tensoring with $\Omega$, hence to zero before tensoring, by the vector-space injection in step 3. This is exactly the criterion for factorization through a closed subscheme. Apply the same argument to inverse and unit. The group identities hold because their composites with the closed immersion into $A_E$ hold, and a closed immersion is a monomorphism. Thus $C_E$ is a closed subgroup scheme in the sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup].

source.place: Appendix A.65–A.66; explicit ideal-factorization and monomorphism argument.

proof.text: The field extension $\Omega/E$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]; its map of spectra is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], and it is quasi-compact since it is affine. Since $(C_E)_\Omega=C$ is smooth, [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] makes $C_E$ smooth over $E$. Also $A_E$ is an abelian variety by [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes its closed subscheme $C_E$ proper. The projection $C\to C_E$ is surjective: apply the same faithfully-flat and spectrum-surjectivity statements on affine charts. If $C_E$ were the union of two nonempty disjoint clopen subsets, their inverse images would be such a decomposition of the connected scheme $C$. Hence $C_E$ is connected and nonempty. Together with step 4 this gives all three properties of an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and step 3 gives the required field and subgroup equality.
